_meta.description: Seed (placeholder) numeric parameters for the BRI fire-resilience credit model. ALL VALUES ARE ENGINEERING-JUDGEMENT SEEDS, not calibrated. They are physically defensible starting points intended to be recalibrated against loss data later. Source structure derives from the BRI fire research doc (docs/fire/); the numbers themselves are invented for the simulation to run.

initiation._doc: Model A — Poisson initiation. lambda_i = lambda_0,c * m_occ * m_proc * m_cond * m_protection * m_history. A fire instantiates for an asset-draw when the Poisson count N_i >= 1.

base_annual_frequency_by_type._doc: lambda_0,c — base annual ignition frequency per asset by CommercialType (events/year).

m_occ_by_status._doc: Occupancy multiplier (range ~0.75-1.30). Occupied buildings have more ignition sources but faster human detection; vacant buildings have fewer sources but also no occupant intervention. Seeds keep occupied as the 1.0 reference.

m_proc_by_type._doc: Process-load multiplier (range ~1.00-2.50) — proxy for ignition-prone processes/equipment by CommercialType. Re-derives the v1 FireLoadRating/IndustrialProcessRisk that v2 CDM removed.

m_proc_business_rates_override._doc: If BusinessRatesCategory indicates a higher-process use, override/raise m_proc. Restaurant => kitchen process load.

m_cond_by_condition._doc: Condition multiplier (range ~0.85-1.40). Poor condition => degraded wiring, deferred maintenance => higher ignition.

m_protection_by_level._doc: Protection multiplier (range ~0.85-1.10) keyed on resilience level. Derived as the mean level index across AutomaticDetectionInstalled, SuppressionSystemsInstalled, EmergencyProceduresTested. Better protection slightly lowers ignition frequency (housekeeping/inspection effect).

m_history._doc: History multiplier (range ~0.90-1.60). Recent fires signal latent unaddressed risk. recent_years = window (years) for 'recent'.

initiation_class_priors_by_type._doc: Categorical over the entry-point / cause class given a fire occurs. Each row sums to 1.0. Order: [InternalElectrical, KitchenOccupant, PlantTechnical, ProcessRelated, BasementService, ExternalExposure, Other]. The class seeds the building entry point used by the progression stage.

progression._doc: Model B/C/D seeds — used by the next build stage (15-min stepwise progression and the point-of-no-return gate). Stored here now so all numeric governance lives in one file.

growth_per_step_intensity._doc: Latent intensity I_t additive growth per 15-min step before suppression bites, by compartmentation quality.

i_crit_by_suppression._doc: Critical intensity threshold I_crit. If I_t crosses this before suppression bites, the chain hits the point of no return (S5 column collapses to ~0). The weak value is set so a poorly-compartmented, weakly-suppressed asset can actually lose the controllability race (PNR reachable around step 5); the strong value is high enough that a well-protected asset suppresses long before I_t approaches it (PNR effectively unreachable).

detection_time_multiplier_by_level._doc: Scales time-to-detect; lower = faster detection. Keyed on AutomaticDetectionInstalled resilience level.

suppression_growth_multiplier_by_level._doc: Scales intensity growth once suppression is active; lower = more effective suppression. Keyed on SuppressionSystemsInstalled resilience level.

passive_effectiveness_ranges._doc: Passive (structural) defence effectiveness in [0,1] mapped across the 5 resilience levels (Not assessed -> Verified). Higher = slows growth / limits spread.

response_effectiveness_ranges._doc: Active response effectiveness in [0,1] across the 5 resilience levels. Higher = faster/more effective external + procedural response.

upper_floor_penalty_per_storey._doc: Height/vertical penalty multiplier applied per storey to suppression difficulty (NumberOfStoreys proxy; commercial schema has no explicit FloorLevelMeters). Interpolated linearly from 1 storey -> range[0] to max_storeys -> range[1]. Applies when suppression can actually engage (internal sprinklers, or external fire-service reach); see fire_service_reach for the height cut-off.

fire_service_reach._doc: External fire-service suppression only reaches up to reach_storeys — the height a fire appliance / aerial ladder can effectively service (~4 storeys, the BRI fire-truck reach). At or below the reach the fire service can mount an effective external attack even with no internal systems. Above the reach, suppression must come from internal sprinklers: a building taller than reach_storeys with no adequate internal suppression never achieves effective suppression (the suppression flag never bites) and runs to the point of no return. internal_suppression_threshold = SuppressionSystemsInstalled level index (0-4) at/above which the asset counts as having effective, height-independent internal sprinklers. no_reach_bite_steps = suppression-bite time (steps) when neither internal sprinklers nor fire-service reach is available — set beyond the step budget so suppression effectively never engages.

timing._doc: Base timing in 15-min steps for the controllability race. detection_base_steps = expected steps from ignition to detection at a neutral detection level; suppression_bite_base_steps = expected steps from detection until active suppression takes effect. The height penalty multiplies the suppression-bite time (harder to reach upper floors).

intensity_dynamics._doc: Knobs governing the latent intensity track I_t. passive_damp_weight scales how much aggregate passive effectiveness slows per-step growth (effective_growth = growth_per_step * (1 - passive_damp_weight * passive_effectiveness)). compartmentation_well_threshold = mean level index (0-4) of CompartmentsProvided+FireStoppingAtPenetrations at/above which growth uses the well_compartmented rate. strong_suppression_threshold = SuppressionSystemsInstalled level index (0-4) at/above which i_crit uses the strong_suppression value.

controllability._doc: Aggregate controllability score in [0,1] combining passive, response and suppression effectiveness; selects which pre-PNR transition matrix is used. weights are normalised over the three components. score >= switch_threshold uses AA_controllable, else weak_controllable. suppression_component maps the SuppressionSystemsInstalled level index (0-4) to [0,1] via idx/4.

transition_matrices._doc: Example 8x8 row-stochastic transition matrices over states [S0..S7]. Row i = P(next state | current state i). The progression stage selects/blends a matrix per step from the asset's controllability state. point_of_no_return zeroes the S5 (Contained) column so the chain is absorbing into {S6, S7}.
